## The question

\vspace{1.5em}

\begin{center}
\Large\bfseries\color{econblue}
How do we attach finite-sample, distribution-free\\[0.1em]
coverage guarantees to any fitted model in R?
\end{center}

\vspace{1em}

\begin{center}
\normalsize\itshape
Eleven methods, one model-agnostic interface, any learner from \texttt{lm} to \texttt{xgboost}.
\end{center}

::: notes
Open with the question, not the package. Predictive intervals in R
are usually parametric or bootstrap. Both assume correct specification
or asymptotics. Conformal prediction asks the analyst for neither.
:::


## Why it matters

- **Regulators** (EU AI Act, FDA SaMD) now require calibrated uncertainty alongside point predictions
- **Clinical prediction** needs per-patient intervals that are valid without model assumptions
- **Credit and insurance** need group-conditional coverage that a marginal guarantee cannot deliver
- **Operations research** needs sequential intervals that adapt when the data-generating process drifts

::: notes
Four distinct stakeholder groups, four live use cases. Point at the
regulatory angle: AI Act and FDA both now treat calibrated uncertainty
as a first-class requirement. 60 seconds.
:::



## What is already out there

- **`probably`** (tidymodels): regression only, no classification, no Jackknife+ or CV+\footnote{\scriptsize Kuhn \& Vaughan (2023), \textit{probably: Tools for Post-Processing Class Probability Estimates}, R package.}
- **`conformalInference`** (GitHub only): research code, not on CRAN, unmaintained since 2019
- **Classification, Mondrian, weighted, ACI**: no prior CRAN implementation at all
- **Bespoke scripts**: most practitioners roll their own, with no shared test harness

\vspace{0.5em}

The gap: **no single CRAN package covers the standard conformal workflow end to end**.

::: notes
Respect existing packages. probably covers a narrow slice well; the
research code is stale. predictset fills the vacuum for classification
and the conditional-coverage variants. 45 seconds.
:::



## What predictset offers

1. **Coverage**: 11 methods spanning split, CV+, Jackknife+, CQR, APS, RAPS, LAC, Mondrian, weighted, ACI, conformal p-values
2. **Interface**: every method takes a formula, a fitted model, or a user-defined train/predict pair; same three-line call across regression and classification
3. **Provenance**: pure R, no compiled code, four runtime imports, 318 tests, CRAN since March 2026

\vspace{0.5em}

Methods follow @angelopoulos2023gentle and the primary sources cited per function\footnote{\scriptsize Angelopoulos \& Bates (2023), \textit{Conformal Prediction: A Gentle Introduction}, Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 16(4).}.

::: notes
Three bullets, three selling points. Emphasise the unified interface:
switching from split conformal to Mondrian is a one-word change. CRAN
presence signals maturity. 45 seconds.
:::

## Central formulas

\vspace{0.3em}

\textbf{Nonconformity score} (absolute residual form):
\begin{equation}
s_i = |y_i - \hat{f}(x_i)|, \qquad i \in \mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{cal}}
\end{equation}

\textbf{Conformal quantile} (calibration order statistic):
\begin{equation}
\hat{q}_\alpha = s_{\left(\lceil (n_{\mathrm{cal}} + 1)(1 - \alpha) \rceil\right)}
\end{equation}

\textbf{Coverage guarantee} (Vovk et al.\ 2005; Lei et al.\ 2018):
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\!\left\{Y_{n+1} \in \hat{C}(X_{n+1})\right\} \;\geq\; 1 - \alpha
\end{equation}

::: notes
Three equations, one idea each. Do not read them aloud. Point at the
order-statistic index and the coverage inequality. The guarantee holds
finite-sample under exchangeability, no model assumptions needed.
60 seconds.
:::



## Package at a glance

::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}

Function families:

- **Regression**: `conformal_split`, `conformal_cv`, `conformal_jackknife`, `conformal_cqr`
- **Classification**: `conformal_aps`, `conformal_raps`, `conformal_lac`
- **Conditional / adaptive**: `conformal_mondrian`, `conformal_mondrian_class`, `conformal_weighted`, `conformal_aci`
- **Diagnostics**: `coverage`, `coverage_by_group`, `coverage_by_bin`, `interval_width`, `set_size`, `conformal_compare`

Deps: `cli`, `grDevices`, `graphics`, `stats`. R $\geq$ 4.1.0.

:::
::: {.column width="40%"}

\begin{block}{Three-tier model interface}
Every method accepts:

1. A formula \texttt{y \~{} .}
2. A fitted \texttt{lm}, \texttt{glm}, \texttt{ranger}
3. A \texttt{make\_model()} wrapper for \texttt{xgboost}, custom learners
\end{block}

:::
:::

::: notes
Two columns. Left lists the 22 exported functions grouped by family.
Right highlights the model interface in the blue block. The three-tier
design is the pitch: no dispatch adaptors, no subclassing. 45 seconds.
:::



## Minimal working example

```r
library(predictset)

# Fit, calibrate, predict: any model, any method, three lines
fit  <- conformal_split(y ~ ., data = train,
                        x_new = x_test, alpha = 0.10)
cov  <- coverage(fit, y_test)
new  <- predict(fit, newdata = future_data)

# Swap method: same call, change one word
fit2 <- conformal_jackknife(y ~ ., data = train,
                            x_new = x_test, alpha = 0.10)
```

\footnotesize
The conformal object caches the fitted model and calibration quantile,
so new data is scored without refitting.

::: notes
Live-read the code. The value is the symmetry: changing from split to
Jackknife+ means replacing one function name. No new arguments, no
separate wrapper. 60 seconds.
:::



## Case study: fairness via group-conditional coverage

**Data.** ProPublica COMPAS recidivism dataset, 6167 defendants in Broward County, Florida, screened 2013-14\footnote{\scriptsize Angwin et al.\ (2016), \textit{Machine Bias}, ProPublica.}.

**Question.** *Can conformal prediction deliver equalised per-group coverage where a marginal guarantee cannot?*

**Why this case.** Canonical benchmark in algorithmic-fairness literature. A 90 per cent marginal guarantee is consistent with 99 per cent coverage on one subgroup and 60 per cent on another. @romano2020malice treat equalised coverage as a minimum fairness standard.

::: notes
Setup only. No results on this slide. Point forward: hero figure
is next. Name the data source, the target, and why Mondrian is the
right tool. 45 seconds.
:::

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[height=0.68\textheight]{figures/hero_figure.pdf}
\end{center}

\vspace{-0.4em}

{\footnotesize\itshape Per-race coverage on COMPAS two-year recidivism at target $1 - \alpha = 0.90$. Marginal APS over-covers both subgroups; Mondrian APS tracks the target per group.}
```

::: notes
The money slide. Ninety seconds. Walk the audience through the two
panels: marginal APS hits the marginal guarantee by over-covering in
both groups; Mondrian APS recovers the per-group target with smaller
sets. This is the single most important fairness property conformal
prediction delivers. Pause before moving on.
:::



## CV+ and Jackknife+ recover width without losing coverage

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[height=0.68\textheight]{figures/fig2_compare.pdf}
\end{center}

\vspace{-0.5em}

{\footnotesize\itshape Mean interval width at target coverage $0.90$. CV+ and Jackknife+ reclaim roughly 9 per cent of the width that split conformal sacrifices by halving the training data.}
```

::: notes
One operational example of the efficiency frontier. Split conformal is
fast but inefficient on small samples. CV+ and Jackknife+ pay model
fits for width. The package prints per-method wall-clock time via
\texttt{conformal\_compare()} so users can make the trade-off
explicitly. 60 seconds.
:::


## What predictset does not yet do

- **No parametric or Bayesian intervals**: use `rstanarm`, `brms`, or base `predict()` for those
- **Time-series dependence**: only ACI is implemented; full sequential-data conformal methods are pending
- **Weighted conformal requires user-supplied weights**: no bundled density-ratio estimator
- **Classification set size depends on base calibration**: miscalibrated probabilities yield larger sets

\vspace{0.5em}

**v0.4.0 roadmap**: conformal procedures for dependent data beyond ACI, likelihood-ratio estimators for weighted conformal, tighter `tidymodels` integration.

::: notes
Honest limitations. Name each one. Frame v0.4.0 as a commitment, not a
vague plan. Users who want Bayesian intervals are already well served
elsewhere; predictset is deliberately not that package. 45 seconds.
:::
